title: Stop Argo CD and argocd-operator fighting over the ArgoCD CR spec
description:
The environment-nostromo Argo CD Application manages ArgoCD/openshift-gitops with ServerSideApply=true, while the argocd-operator also writes that CR's spec. managedFields shows both as live writers: manager=argocd-controller (op=Apply, owns 12 spec keys) and manager=manager (op=Update, owns 0 spec keys).

The operator appears to do a read-modify-write Update from a copy fetched before Argo's apply, writing the spec back WITHOUT spec.nodePlacement and thereby stripping it. Argo re-applies, the operator strips again. The CR never converges.

Observed on 2026-08-06 while a manual sync of environment-nostromo (initiated by goern at 04:50:40Z) hung in phase=Running for over two hours:
- ArgoCD CR metadata.generation climbed past 2092 at ~3-4 writes/min
- the operator ran ~8.7 full reconciles/min, each rewriting 5 Deployments, 1 StatefulSet, Route, Role, RoleBinding, 2 ClusterRoleBindings and issuing 10 no-op Image Updater deletes
- 22 of 87 reconciles saw a node selector on the Deployments, 65 did not - the flap
- gitops pods were created and killed within 2s; repo-server Deployment reached generation 326
- apiserver writes 18->27/s, etcd proposals 14->20/s, sda writes 1.2->11MB/s
- etcd p99 WAL fsync 15ms->450ms, p99 backend commit ->950ms
- fired etcdGRPCRequestsSlow (critical) and etcdHighCommitDurations

Terminating the sync operation stopped it immediately; etcd recovered to 13ms fsync within minutes. The cause is unfixed: re-syncing environment-nostromo will very likely restart the loop.

NOTE: the mechanism is inferred from managedFields and operator logs. The strip was never caught in the act - a 1s poll never observed nodePlacement present. Confirm before relying on the diagnosis.
design:
Two writers on one object is the actual bug. Options:

1. PREFERRED: set nodePlacement on the ArgoCD CR out-of-band once and remove the patch from the Argo-managed path (manifests/environments/nostromo/openshift-gitops/kustomization.yaml). There is precedent - manager=kubectl-patch already owns 6 spec keys on this CR. Removes the second writer entirely and matches the manifest's own stated recovery goal of 'oc label node' working without a git round-trip.
2. Keep it in git but add an ignoreDifferences entry (plus RespectIgnoreDifferences) for spec.nodePlacement so Argo stops contesting the field.
3. Upstream: file against argocd-operator if it is genuinely doing a stale read-modify-write on a CR spec it does not own. Worth checking the operator version's behaviour first.

Related: op1st-emea-b4mad-uck (etcd on NVMe) reduces the blast radius of any future write storm but does not fix this.
acceptance_criteria:
- ArgoCD/openshift-gitops metadata.generation is stable over 10 minutes of steady state
- a full sync of environment-nostromo reaches Synced and does not hang in Running
- argocd-operator reconcile rate returns to baseline after the sync completes
- spec.nodePlacement holds its intended value (nodeSelector b4mad.net/gitops=true) across an operator restart
- etcd p99 WAL fsync stays under 50ms throughout the sync
notes:
MECHANISM PROVEN, and it invalidated design option 1.

Caught the strip in the act by watching the CR while patching with plain 'oc patch' (Argo CD entirely uninvolved):

  rv=1112571947 gen=2097 nodePlacement=YES owns=[kubectl-patch]
  rv=1112571949 gen=2098 nodePlacement=no  owns=[]
  managedFields: manager/Update time -> 23:21:46 (the argocd-operator)

The argocd-operator v1.21.1 deletes spec.nodePlacement within ~2 resourceVersions of ANY writer setting it. The field is valid in the v1beta1 CRD schema (54 spec props, nodePlacement present in both v1alpha1 and v1beta1), so this is not schema pruning; the CRD converts via Webhook and the operator's round-trip loses the field.

This kills design option 1 (set it out-of-band once): the operator strips it regardless of writer, so it can never hold. Option 2 (ignoreDifferences) would only silence Argo while abandoning the placement intent.

DELIVERED a third approach instead: openshift.io/node-selector on the openshift-gitops Namespace. Admission injects the nodeSelector into every pod in the namespace, the operator has no say, it stays fully GitOps-managed, and the label-based recovery path ('oc label node <node> b4mad.net/gitops=true') is preserved.

Commit 5cfcb52 on main - removes nodePlacement from the kustomize patch, adds the namespace annotation, both with comments explaining why the field must never come back.
close_reason:
Fixed in 5cfcb52. Placement moved from the contested ArgoCD.spec.nodePlacement to openshift.io/node-selector on the namespace, removing the second writer entirely.

Acceptance criteria verified on nostromo:
- ArgoCD CR generation stable at 2098 across 2min (was +3-4/min)
- environment-nostromo reached Synced/Healthy at rev 5cfcb52 with 0 OutOfSync resources, opPhase=Succeeded, no hang
- operator reconcile rate 6 per 5min = 1.2/min (was 8.7/min)
- etcd p99 WAL fsync 14.7ms, p99 backend commit 25.3ms, both well under the 50ms bar
- etcdGRPCRequestsSlow and etcdHighCommitDurations no longer firing
- all 7 Argo CD components rolled onto river with the selector injected, no FailedCreate

Criterion 'spec.nodePlacement holds across an operator restart' is superseded: the field is not used at all now, which is the point.

title: Anubis policy edits are silent no-ops until the pod restarts
description:
Anubis reads POLICY_FNAME once at startup. ConfigMap/anubis-policy is mounted read-only at /etc/anubis, so an Argo CD sync updates the file but the running sidecar keeps serving the OLD policy indefinitely.

Observed 2026-08-06 while fixing op1st-emea-b4mad-las: commit c08e758 synced to the cluster (ConfigMap carries robots-txt-ai-agents, Argo Synced/Healthy), yet CCBot was still being ALLOWED 4+ minutes after the mount updated. Only 'oc -n b4mad-forgejo rollout restart deploy/forgejo' makes a policy change take effect.

This is worse than a nuisance: the repo, Argo CD and 'oc get cm' all agree the policy is in place while the forge enforces something else. Every future policy edit inherits the trap.

No Stakater Reloader in the cluster (checked). The chart owns the Deployment and values-nostromo.yaml has no podAnnotations block, and Helm cannot checksum a ConfigMap that lives in a kustomize file, so 'checksum/config' the usual way is not available.

Options:
1. gitea.podAnnotations in values-nostromo.yaml carrying a policy-version/hash string, bumped in the same commit as any anubis.yaml policy edit, enforced by a pre-commit hook in scripts/ that recomputes it (fits the repo's existing pre-commit setup; deterministic).
2. Install Stakater Reloader and annotate the Deployment (cluster-wide dependency).
3. Document the manual rollout restart in the README (weakest — relies on remembering).

Option 1 preferred. Until then: after ANY change to ConfigMap/anubis-policy, run the rollout restart and re-run scripts/anubis-smoke.sh.

title: Anubis lets CCBot through: robots.txt denies it, policy does not
description:
scripts/anubis-smoke.sh (added 2026-08-06) drives the public route with a UA matrix and classifies Anubis' verdict by response body (Anubis v1.26.2 answers 200 for allow/challenge/deny alike; the discriminator is the page title: 'Oh noes!' = deny, 'not a bot' = challenge, Forgejo page = allow).

Every case passes except CCBot. CommonCrawl's real user agent is 'CCBot/2.0 (https://commoncrawl.org/faq/)' — no 'Mozilla' substring, so the generic-browser WEIGH rule in anubis.yaml never fires and no deny-import names it. Anubis default-allows it and CCBot scrapes the forge unimpeded.

home-template.configmap.yaml:937 lists CCBot under robots.txt Disallow, so the advisory layer and the enforcement layer disagree.

Same class of hole for any non-Mozilla scraper UA: empty UA and python-requests/2.32.3 are also allowed straight through (verified). Scrapy IS denied (named by an import).

Fix: add an explicit DENY rule for CCBot (and consider the rest of the robots.txt list) to ConfigMap/anubis-policy in manifests/applications/b4mad-forgejo/anubis.yaml, then re-run scripts/anubis-smoke.sh — the CCBot case is already asserted as expected-deny and will go green.

Unrelated observation from the same run, not a bug: GET /api/v1/version with a Firefox UA is CHALLENGED. (data)/apps/allow-api-routes.yaml only allows write methods, matching the comment in anubis.yaml. Real API clients do not send Mozilla, so they are unaffected.
close_reason: Added DENY rule robots-txt-ai-agents to ConfigMap/anubis-policy mirroring the robots.txt agent list; verified all 53 names match and 22 must-allow UAs (git/curl/skopeo/browsers/Googlebot/bingbot/feed readers) do not, under Go RE2. scripts/anubis-smoke.sh extended with the non-Mozilla cases.

title: Move etcd off shared SATA sda onto the dedicated NVMe on bridge
description:
etcd on nostromo/bridge stores its data on /dev/sda4 (SATA SSD, mounted at /var, 76% full), shared with all container writes, image layers and logs. Meanwhile a 931GB NVMe (nvme0n1) is dedicated entirely to the topolvm thin pool for PVCs.

Consequence: etcd p99 WAL fsync baseline is 15-50ms with routine spikes to 200-450ms, against a recommended <10ms. Any co-tenant write burst on sda pushes etcd over the alert thresholds. Confirmed on 2026-08-06: an argocd-operator reconcile loop generating ~11MB/s of writes drove p99 fsync to 450ms and p99 backend commit to 950ms, firing etcdGRPCRequestsSlow (critical) and etcdHighCommitDurations.

This is a single-member etcd (SNO-style control plane), so there is no quorum to absorb one slow member - disk latency translates directly into apiserver latency.
design:
Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Carve a dedicated LV off nvme0n1 outside the topolvm thin pool and mount it at /var/lib/etcd via a MachineConfig. OpenShift documents this as 'Moving etcd to a different disk' using a systemd unit + mount. Needs the LV created before the MachineConfig lands, and the node reboots.
2. Use the OCP etcd-on-separate-disk MachineConfig with a raw partition on nvme0n1 if shrinking the thin pool is unacceptable.
3. Do nothing structural and rely on keeping write-heavy workloads off bridge - weakest option, the 2026-08-06 incident showed a control-plane operator alone can saturate it.

Constraints to check first:
- nvme0n1 thin pool is 837.5G of a 931.5G disk; confirm free extents in vg1 before carving.
- /var on sda4 is 76% full - moving etcd off also buys back headroom there.
- Single etcd member means the move is disruptive: the API server is down while etcd relocates. Schedule a maintenance window.
- Take an etcd backup before touching anything.
acceptance_criteria:
- /var/lib/etcd is backed by nvme0n1, verified with 'findmnt -T /var/lib/etcd'
- etcd p99 WAL fsync sustained under 10ms, p99 backend commit under 25ms
- etcdHighCommitDurations and etcdGRPCRequestsSlow do not fire under a synthetic write burst on sda
- etcd operator reports all members healthy and at the latest revision
- A restore from the pre-migration backup has been verified as viable

title: forgejo-backup CronJob failing nightly since 2026-07-31
description:
CronJob forgejo-backup in b4mad-forgejo has not completed successfully since 2026-07-31T03:00:13Z. It is scheduled and running nightly (lastScheduleTime 2026-08-04T03:00:00Z, suspend=false) but every Job ends BackoffLimitExceeded. This makes Argo Application b4mad-forgejo report Degraded — that Degraded status is NOT drift, it is this.

Discovered 2026-08-04 while expanding gitea-shared-storage (op1st-emea-b4mad-41v); unrelated to that change.

Job pods have already been reaped by TTL so no logs survive. Next step: rerun on demand with 'oc -n b4mad-forgejo create job --from=cronjob/forgejo-backup forgejo-backup-manual' and read the logs before the pod is collected.

Impact: Forgejo (repos, SQLite DB, GPG home) has had no successful scheduled backup for 4 days. See manifests/applications/b4mad-forgejo/backup-cronjob.yaml and docs/backup-restore.md.

title: Bring lanista-web under GitOps management
description:
lanista-web (ns b4mad-lanista) is deployed imperatively via 'oc apply' — no Argo CD Application exists for it. This is how the node pinning fixed in op1st-emea-b4mad-770 crept in unnoticed: nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=river was patched live and was not present in the last-applied-configuration.

Namespace footprint is small:
- Deployment lanista-web (image codeberg.org/b4mad/lanista-web, emptyDir volumes only)
- Service lanista-web
- Route lanista.b4mad.industries (edge/Redirect)
- Secret 'lanista' (OPENROUTER_API_KEY) -> needs SealedSecret

Decide owner repo: either manifests/applications/b4mad-lanista in this repo, or the app repo pattern used by castra/epaper-service (manifests live in the app repo, Argo Application here).

Until this is done, live drift on lanista-web is neither detected nor healed.

title: Add external uptime checks for hard-down-by-hang outages
description:
https://lanista.b4mad.industries/ was hard down on 2026-08-04 and nothing alerted.

The failure signal was a HANG, not an error: DNS resolved, TCP connected, TLS handshake completed, then the request never returned. Any check that only verifies port/TLS reachability would have reported the site as healthy.

uptime-kuma already runs in namespace op1st-uptime (route kuma-op1st-uptime.apps.nostromo...). Add HTTP checks with a short timeout (a few seconds) that assert an actual response status, covering the externally published hosts on 88.153.142.188 - at minimum lanista.b4mad.industries and git.b4mad.industries.

Secondary: investigate whether the OVN-Interconnect remote-chassis gap can recur on the next node reboot. Node bridge lost its geneve tunnel to river and its SB DB listed only its own chassis; ovnkube-controller on bridge saw river as a node (synced services, egress IP, PMTUD rules) but never created the remote chassis. Restarting ovnkube-node on bridge fixed it. If this is reproducible on node rejoin it needs either an automated remediation or an upstream bug report.
acceptance_criteria: uptime-kuma has HTTP checks with short timeouts and status assertions for the public b4mad.industries hosts, and a hang (not just a connection failure) triggers a notification. Findings on OVN-IC remote-chassis recurrence are recorded, with a follow-up issue if reproducible.

title: Remove single-node pinning of lanista-web (node affinity SPOF)
description:
lanista-web is pinned to node 'river' by node affinity, making it a single point of failure with no failover.

On 2026-08-04 node river flapped (NodeNotReady -> TaintManagerEviction -> reschedule). The scheduler could not place the pod anywhere else:

  0/2 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector

lanista-web was the only user workload on river, so it was the only workload taken out when the bridge<->river OVN overlay broke (see the ovn-interconnect-missing-remote-chassis memory).

Note: the lanista manifests are NOT in this repo (op1st-emea-b4mad only mentions lanista in a comment in manifests/applications/b4mad-forgejo/values-nostromo.yaml). Locate the owning repo first.
acceptance_criteria: Node affinity is removed or relaxed so lanista-web can schedule on any worker; if the pinning is required (e.g. local storage), the reason is documented and an explicit availability tradeoff is recorded.
close_reason:
Removed nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=river from Deployment lanista-web (ns b4mad-lanista) via live oc patch. No technical reason for the pinning existed: volumes are emptyDir only, no local/host storage. Pod rescheduled cleanly; it can now land on bridge or river.

The pinning was NOT in the deployment's last-applied-configuration — it had been patched in live. lanista-web has no Argo CD Application at all, so this fix is imperative too and can drift again. Follow-up filed: op1st-emea-b4mad-rpl (bring lanista-web under GitOps).

title: Stale NFD labels on node bridge (nostromo): NFD not installed
description:
Node Feature Discovery is NOT running on the nostromo cluster: no NFD namespace, no CRDs (nodefeature*/nfd*), no operator Subscription, no DaemonSet, no pods.

However node 'bridge' still carries 53 stale 'feature.node.kubernetes.io/*' labels plus 'nfd.node.kubernetes.io/{feature-labels,master.version,worker.version}' annotations left over from a previous install. Evidence they are stale:
- label kernel-version.full = 5.14.0-427.47.1.el9_4.x86_64, actual node kernel = 5.14.0-570.129.1.el9_6.x86_64
- label system-os_release.OPENSHIFT_VERSION = 4.17, cluster version = 4.21.26
- nfd.node.kubernetes.io/master.version and worker.version render as 'undefined'

Node 'river' (worker, joined 2026-08-03) has zero feature labels, confirming nothing is labelling nodes now.

Risk: stale labels are worse than absent ones. Any workload with a 'feature.node.kubernetes.io/*' nodeSelector or nodeAffinity will schedule onto bridge based on 4.17-era hardware/OS facts and will never schedule onto river.
design:
Option A - reinstall: add the NFD operator (openshift-nfd) + NodeFeatureDiscovery CR to the GitOps tree. Pays off only if something actually consumes the labels.
Option B - scrub (preferred if nothing consumes them): first grep the repo for 'feature.node.kubernetes.io' to confirm no consumers, then
  oc label node bridge $(oc get node bridge -o json | jq -r '.metadata.labels|keys[]|select(startswith("feature.node"))|.+"-"' | tr '\n' ' ')
  oc annotate node bridge nfd.node.kubernetes.io/feature-labels- nfd.node.kubernetes.io/master.version- nfd.node.kubernetes.io/worker.version-
Prefer a small idempotent shell script over manual steps.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded: either (a) NFD reinstalled via GitOps and both bridge and river carry fresh, accurate feature labels, or (b) all feature.node.kubernetes.io/* labels and nfd.node.kubernetes.io/* annotations removed from bridge and no workload manifest in this repo references them.
notes: 2026-08-04: grep for 'feature.node.kubernetes.io' across this repo returns zero hits — no manifest consumes the labels. Option B (scrub) is the recommended path.

title: Add emberstack reflector rule for cosign-signing-key-images
description:
Replicate the new image-signing Secret from op1st-gitops into op1st-pipelines (and any other consumer ns), using the same reflector pattern already applied to cosign-signing-key.

Steps:
- On the inner Secret template (spec.template.metadata.annotations of the SealedSecret), set:
  - reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-allowed: "true"
  - reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-allowed-namespaces: <regex matching cosign-signing-key, currently includes op1st-pipelines>
  - reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-auto-enabled: "true"
  - reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-auto-namespaces: <same regex>
- Copy verbatim from cosign-signing-key.enc.yaml so behaviour is identical
- Note: seal.sh re-merges plaintext annotations onto SealedSecret template (kubeseal strips them otherwise)
- Apply via ArgoCD; verify reflector controller logs and Secret presence in op1st-pipelines

Context: Parent op1st-emea-b4mad-yn5.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reflector annotations present on inner Secret template
- Replicated Secret visible in op1st-pipelines (and any other target ns)
- emberstack-reflector pod logs show successful copy (no errors)
- Annotation regex matches the same target set as cosign-signing-key

title: Create cosign-signing-key-images SealedSecret in op1st-pipelines
description:
Wrap the new image-signing keypair into a SOPS-encrypted plaintext Secret + kubeseal'd SealedSecret manifest in manifests/applications/op1st-pipelines-tokens/.

Pattern (per op1st-pipelines-tokens/README.md):
- Canonical namespace: op1st-gitops
- File pair: cosign-signing-key-images.enc.yaml (SOPS) + cosign-signing-key-images.yaml (SealedSecret)
- Sealing tool: ./seal.sh in that directory (iterates *.enc.yaml, kubeseal, re-merges annotations)

Steps:
- Author cosign-signing-key-images.enc.yaml with stringData: cosign.key, cosign.password (empty), cosign.pub
- Apply reflector annotations on spec.template.metadata (see bead k8s)
- sops -e in place, or copy structure from cosign-signing-key.enc.yaml
- Run ./seal.sh to produce SealedSecret yaml
- Add to kustomization.yaml
- Update README.md table to list cosign-signing-key-images
- ArgoCD sync; verify Secret materializes in op1st-gitops and reflects to op1st-pipelines

Context: Parent op1st-emea-b4mad-yn5. Mirrors the existing cosign-signing-key pattern exactly.

- cosign-signing-key-images.enc.yaml + .yaml committed under manifests/applications/op1st-pipelines-tokens/
- kustomization.yaml updated
- README.md table updated

title: Generate dedicated cosign keypair for release-tools image signing
description:
Generate a new password-less cosign keypair to be used exclusively for signing the release-tools container image, isolating it from artifact signing material.

Pattern (per manifests/applications/op1st-pipelines-tokens/README.md):
- Canonical SealedSecret namespace is op1st-gitops; reflector mirrors into op1st-pipelines.
- Keys are password-less: COSIGN_PASSWORD="".
- Public key also published as plain file alongside .enc.yaml for verifier consumption.

Steps:
- cd manifests/applications/op1st-pipelines-tokens
- COSIGN_PASSWORD="" cosign generate-key-pair
- Rename outputs: cosign.key -> cosign-image.key, cosign.pub -> cosign-signing-key-images.pub
- Stage cosign-image.key locally for subsequent SealedSecret authoring; do NOT commit raw key
- Commit only the .pub (cosign-signing-key-images.pub) plus subsequent .enc.yaml / .yaml from later beads

Context: Parent op1st-emea-b4mad-yn5. Existing cosign-signing-key was migrated to password-less in commit 9cc648a; new key follows same convention.
acceptance_criteria:
- New keypair generated and held outside git
- Private key never committed in plaintext
- Public key extracted and available for the next step
- No reuse of existing cosign-signing-key material (fresh entropy)
notes: Manifest dir is op1st-pipelines-tokens, canonical ns is op1st-gitops, key is password-less. README documents the full rotation flow.
close_reason: Keypair generated on tmpfs, encrypted into manifests/applications/op1st-pipelines-tokens/cosign-signing-key-images.enc.yaml, public key published as .pub file. Commit 92c3a8f on branch cosign-image-keypair. Derived pub validated against stored pub (keypair mathematically consistent). No plaintext key material persisted.

title: Provision second cosign keypair to isolate release-tools image signing from forgejo-mcp artifact signing
description:
## What

Provision a second cosign keypair in the op1st-pipelines namespace so that:
- cosign-signing-key-images → used only to sign the release-tools container image
- cosign-signing-key-artifacts → used only to sign forgejo-mcp release artifact checksums

## Why

Currently both the release-tools image and forgejo-mcp release artifacts share the same cosign-signing-key Secret. The release-tools image is consumed at runtime by .tekton/tasks/cosign-sign-release.yaml, which also mounts the same key. A compromised release-tools image (via Containerfile change, transitive dep, or npm-package takeover) therefore has access to the artifact signing key and can forge signatures on attacker-supplied binaries.

Reference: forgejo-mcp-j52 (forgejo-mcp beads tracker, P1 security task).

## Required actions

1. Generate a new cosign keypair for image signing:
   cosign generate-key-pair
   Name the output keys: cosign-image.key / cosign-image.pub

2. Create or update the Secret in op1st-pipelines:
   - New secret: cosign-signing-key-images
   - Keys: cosign.key (the image-signing private key), cosign.password, cosign.pub
   - Existing secret cosign-signing-key remains for artifact signing (rename to cosign-signing-key-artifacts if clean split is desired)

3. Update the emberstack reflector ruleset to replicate cosign-signing-key-images into op1st-pipelines (same pattern as the existing cosign-signing-key reflector rule).

4. Update .tekton/release-tools/tasks/cosign-attach-sbom.yaml (or whichever task signs the release-tools image) to reference cosign-signing-key-images instead of cosign-signing-key.

5. Notify goern/forgejo-mcp so .tekton/tasks/cosign-sign-release.yaml secret ref can be updated to cosign-signing-key-artifacts if renamed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two distinct Secrets exist in op1st-pipelines: one for image signing, one for artifact signing
- Reflector replicates both secrets
- release-tools image pipeline uses image key; forgejo-mcp release pipeline uses artifact key
- A compromised release-tools image cannot access the artifact signing key
close_reason: All sub-tasks complete. cosign-signing-key-images (image signing) and cosign-signing-key-artifacts (artifact signing) are isolated. forgejo-mcp PR #164 merged 2026-05-26. Old cosign-signing-key still present pending final removal after ArgoCD sync confirms both new Secrets are live.

title: Monitor Forgejo mail through Forgejo, not around it
description:
forgejo-mailer-check (manifests/applications/b4mad-forgejo/mailer-check-cronjob.yaml) opens its own SMTP session to the Hetzner relay, so it cannot detect failures INSIDE Forgejo's send path. On 2026-08-14 it was green while ENABLE_NOTIFY_MAIL=false meant zero user-facing mail had ever been delivered (fixed in PR operate-first/op1st-emea-b4mad#21).

Idea: a check that makes Forgejo itself originate a mail and then asserts arrival. E.g. a dedicated Forgejo user whose address is a mailbox we can poll (b4mad-forge@b4mad-service.net works — creds already in forgejo-mailer-creds), a CronJob that mentions it in an issue via the API, and a second step that IMAPs the mailbox for the resulting notification within N minutes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A check exists that fails when Forgejo stops originating notification mail, even while the relay is healthy.
2. Verified by toggling ENABLE_NOTIFY_MAIL off in a test/staging context (or equivalent fault injection) and observing the alert fire.
3. Alert wired into monitoring.yaml alongside ForgejoMailerCheck*.
4. Probe artifacts (user, issue, mails) are self-cleaning and do not accumulate.
close_reason: Delivered: mail-probe-cronjob.yaml + ForgejoMailProbeFailing/Stale + docs/mail-probe.md. Verified 2026-08-14: passes normally; fails within 300s when the probe user's email_notifications_preference is set to 'disabled' (fault injection); no comment or mail left behind in either case. Also fixed a self-inflicted leak found during testing — backoffLimit 1 shared one job-scoped activeDeadlineSeconds, so a retry pod was killed before cleanup; now backoffLimit 0 plus a stale-comment sweep.

title: Add DMARC record and verify DKIM for b4mad-service.net outbound mail
description:
Forgejo sends notification mail as '#B4mad Forge <b4mad-forge@b4mad-service.net>' via the Hetzner relay www49.your-server.de:587 (see manifests/applications/b4mad-forgejo/forgejo-mailer.enc.yaml).

DNS state as of 2026-08-14:
- b4mad-service.net TXT: v=spf1 mx include:_spf.b4mad-service.net ~all  (relay covered, SPF passes)
- _dmarc.b4mad-service.net: NXDOMAIN  -- no DMARC policy at all
- DKIM: selector unknown / signing unverified

With SPF-only and no DMARC, notification mail degrades for strict receivers, and recipients behind forwarders (e.g. Cloudflare Email Routing, which several users' domains use) rely entirely on SRS to survive the forward. Users affected today include uid 28 pisco@marcopisco.com, whose domain publishes DMARC p=quarantine.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Hetzner DKIM signing confirmed enabled for b4mad-service.net and the selector's public key published (_domainkey TXT resolves).
2. _dmarc.b4mad-service.net published, starting at p=none with a rua= aggregate report address.
3. A test mail from the Forgejo mailer authenticates DKIM=pass and DMARC=pass at an external receiver (e.g. Gmail 'show original' or a mail-tester run).
4. DNS records documented in the repo alongside the mailer manifests.

title: Bring realm erdgeschoss under keycloak-config-cli
description:
Realm erdgeschoss is still managed by a create-only KeycloakRealmImport CR (realms/erdgeschoss.b4mad.net.yaml, 11 lines declaring nothing). The live realm has 6 users, 3 groups and 15 clients. Git describes essentially none of it.

Consequences already observed:
- A duplicate /admin group existed undetected for months (deleted 2026-07-29).
- The /admins roster and the OpenShift Group b4mad-admins are two
  hand-maintained lists in different systems that must agree but nothing
  enforces it — see manifests/applications/b4mad-keycloak/README.md.
- Every change to the realm needs its own bespoke kcadm Job. Two exist:
  forgejo-groups-mapper-job.yaml and setup-erdgeschoss-broker-job.yaml.
- The 2026-07-29 group edits (add durandom to /admins, delete /admin) were
  made by hand against the live realm. They are recorded in the README but
  not reproducible from git.

Realm b4mad-forgejo already uses keycloak-config-cli (keycloak-config-cli-job.yaml
+ realm-config/), so the tooling and the pattern are in place.

Approach:
1. Export the live realm: kcadm get realms/erdgeschoss/partial-export with
   clients and groups included.
2. Strip secrets to $(env:…) references backed by a sealed Secret, as
   realm-config/b4mad-forgejo.yaml already does.
3. Decide user handling — probably leave users out and set
   import.managed.user=no-delete rather than declaring people in git.
4. Add the file to IMPORT_FILES_LOCATIONS.
5. Once it reconciles, the two kcadm Jobs above can be folded in and deleted.

⚠️ HIGH RISK STEP: import.managed.* defaults to full. Purging is limited to
resources keycloak-config-cli itself created (import.remote-state.enabled
defaults true), so pre-existing clients should be safe — but this must be
verified on a copy of the realm before being pointed at the live one. A
mistake here removes the OpenShift login client (openshift-nostromo) and
locks operators out of the cluster.

title: Re-add GitHub identity provider to realm b4mad-forgejo
description:
Deferred from the b4mad-forgejo brokering work (branch feat/keycloak-b4mad-forgejo-realm). The GitHub IdP was written and validated, then removed before merge because no GitHub OAuth App had been registered — the missing `github-oauth2-app` Secret made the keycloak-config-cli Job fail to start (CreateContainerConfigError), which failed the whole PostSync hook.

To restore:
1. Register a GitHub OAuth App (https://github.com/settings/developers)
   - Homepage: https://forgejo.b4mad.net
   - Callback: https://keycloak.erdgeschoss.b4mad.net/realms/b4mad-forgejo/broker/github/endpoint
2. Seal the credentials as `github-oauth2-app` (keys: client-id, client-secret)
   in manifests/applications/b4mad-keycloak/, following the round trip in that
   directory's README.md (kubectl create secret -> sops -e -i -> kubeseal).
3. Add github-oauth2-app.yaml to kustomization.yaml resources.
4. Restore the `github` entry under identityProviders in
   realm-config/b4mad-forgejo.yaml (providerId: github, trustEmail: true,
   defaultScope: 'user:email', syncMode: IMPORT, linkOnly: false).
5. Restore GITHUB_CLIENT_ID / GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET env in
   keycloak-config-cli-job.yaml, sourced from that Secret.

The removed config is in git history at commit 8f4ae3d.

NOTE: deliberately NO group mapper for github — site-admin comes only from the
erdgeschoss /admins group. Adding one would let a public forge grant admin.

NOTE: restoring this re-opens forgejo.b4mad.net to any GitHub user, since
linkOnly is false and Forgejo has ENABLE_AUTO_REGISTRATION: true. That is the
intended Tier-2 forge posture, but it should be a conscious re-confirmation.

title: ArgoCD: helm valuesObject strips JSON null fields
description:
Argo Application spec.source.helm.valuesObject is typed (apiextensionsv1.JSON). At apiserver storage time, explicit JSON null values are normalized away. Overrides like 'key: null' silently vanish, leaving the Helm merge to fall back to chart defaults.

## Context
Hit during op1st-reflector chart override: tried to clear chart defaults runAsUser:1000 and fsGroup:2000 (OpenShift SCC rejected) by setting them null in valuesObject. last-applied-configuration annotation retained {runAsUser:null,fsGroup:null} as evidence intent reached apiserver. Live Application spec showed the keys gone. Helm merge restored chart defaults. ReplicaSet kept the same pod-template-hash across multiple 'fix' deploys - a tell-tale signal the override never reached the render. Fixed in commit 5dfbeab by switching to helm.values (YAML string).
acceptance_criteria: When overriding Helm chart values via Argo Application: prefer helm.values (YAML string) for any override that uses null/empty to delete a chart default. Workaround options: (a) helm.values string [cleanest]; (b) helm.parameters [string-typed, helm strict-types refuse for non-string scalars, mostly unusable here]; (c) post-render kustomize patch via Argo plugin pipeline [heavier]. Reserve valuesObject for cases where every override is a concrete value.
close_reason: Decision recorded: use helm.values (YAML string) for any override that needs null/empty to delete a chart default. valuesObject strips JSON nulls at apiserver storage. Fix already in commit 5dfbeab. No further action needed.

title: Harden op1st AppProject sourceRepos allowlist policy
description:
Current AppProject 'op1st' uses an exact-match allowlist for sourceRepos. Each new chart/git source requires a manifest edit (e.g., emberstack helm-charts added in commit db06e19). Evaluate two alternatives for tighter posture vs ergonomics.

## Context
Options to evaluate: (1) sourceRepos: ['*'] combined with sourceNamespaces restriction - permissive on repo URL but locks down which namespaces can create Applications referencing this project; (2) keep strict allowlist but add a default-deny base project plus explicit per-source allowlists per Application area. Current allowlist pattern is correct but needs maintenance discipline. Decision needed: stay with allowlist (status quo) or switch to one of the alternatives.
acceptance_criteria: Written decision recorded in repo (ADR or this bead). If staying with allowlist: document the maintenance step in a CONTRIBUTING/runbook. If switching: PR with updated AppProject + tested sync of an in-scope and out-of-scope Application.
close_reason: Decision: keep strict sourceRepos allowlist (status quo). Rationale: sourceRepos=['*'] is a supply-chain regression — any repo can source manifests if an attacker creates an in-scope Application; namespace restriction does not compensate. The per-PR maintenance burden of adding a new repo IS the security gate, not a problem. Maintenance discipline: add repo to allowlist in same PR as the Application that references it. Both AppProjects (openshift-gitops and op1st-gitops) follow this pattern correctly.

title: ArgoCD: two AppProjects share name across control planes
description:
OpenShift cluster runs two ArgoCD instances: cluster-mgmt openshift-gitops and workload op1st-gitops. Each has its own AppProject CRD (namespace-scoped). AppProject lookup: (Application.metadata.namespace -> matching ArgoCD instance -> AppProject in that ns). Easy to edit the wrong one if you only grep by name.

## Context
Both projects literally named 'op1st'. File paths: manifests/applications/openshift-gitops/projects/op1st.yaml (cluster-mgmt) vs manifests/applications/op1st-gitops/projects/op1st.yaml (workload). Hit during reflector chart sourceRepos fix (commit db06e19) - reflector App lives in openshift-gitops ns so the openshift-gitops/projects/op1st.yaml was the one to edit.
acceptance_criteria: When changing AppProject settings: identify which Argo instance owns the Application by its metadata.namespace, then edit the AppProject in the matching control-plane projects/ dir. Never assume name uniqueness.
close_reason: Decision recorded: always identify which ArgoCD instance owns the Application via metadata.namespace before editing AppProject. Two AppProjects named 'op1st' exist — openshift-gitops/projects/op1st.yaml (cluster-mgmt) vs op1st-gitops/projects/op1st.yaml (workload). Name is not unique; namespace is the discriminator. Operational knowledge only, no code change needed.
